title: Predictive Regional Preference & Failover Playground
content:
Status and intent:
Playground for mixing predictive (model-driven) regional preference with classical probe-driven GeoDNS/Anycast failover. Goal is to reduce tail latency violations and cross-region egress cost during localized degradation, with minimal control-plane churn and easy rollback to simpler heuristics.

Context / motivation:
- We already have probe-driven steering (health probes + pref tables) and Anycast for lowest-latency routes, but during partial infra flaps probes are often noisy and cause thrashing.
- Some customers see repeated minor degradations in eu-west that probes flip multiple times a minute; user-facing SLOs spike and costs increase due to hedging.
- Hypothesis: short-term latency trends plus lightweight predictive model can suppress unnecessary regional ejections and choose safer failover targets that balance latency and cost.

Core idea (sketch):
1) Maintain three inputs per region: real-time probe health (p), rolling latency quantiles (q50/q95), and a short-horizon predicted latency delta (d) from an online predictor.
2) Compute a confidence-weighted preference score S = w_p * (1 - p) + w_q * normalized(q95) + w_d * normalized(d). Lower S => higher preference.
3) Use S to:
   - Set GeoDNS weights (soft steering) with TTL hints;
   - Drive Anycast origin reprovisioning decisions (where feasible) or prefer closest healthy POP in routing table;
   - Trigger failover circuit-breakers only when S crosses a higher threshold for T_fail seconds (avoid flip-flop).

Predictor details (lightweight online model):
- Inputs: last N latency samples (per-region moving window, 1s resolution), probe success ratio, CPU/GPU utilization (if available), recent error-rate spikes (5xx ratio), and a binary degradation flag from infra alerts.
- Model: small LSTM or exponentially weighted moving average with feature transforms; primary aim is sign and magnitude of delta over 30–120s horizon rather than absolute accuracy.
- Training: offline on 12 months of telemetry, then warm-start online updates using streaming SGD with strict rate limits to avoid model drift.
- Fallback: if model confidence < threshold, revert to probe-only logic.

Control-plane integration patterns:
- Keep control plane responsibilities minimal: predictor can live in a regional telemetry service; it emits per-region scores to a steering API.
- Steering API aggregates scores and outputs per-POP weights. GeoDNS service consumes these weights and translates to DNS weights and TTLs.
- All changes are versioned and audit-logged to allow immediate rollback.

Failover semantics and hysteresis: (why this differs from current playbooks)
- Dual-thresholds: a soft threshold where traffic is gradually reweighted over a smoothing window (e.g., 60–180s), and a hard threshold where a circuit-breaker marks a region as ejected for a longer cool-down (e.g., 10m).
- Stochastic dampening: on repeated short spikes, we require k-of-m windows to avoid small bursts causing an ejection.
- Cost-aware tie-breaking: when choosing between candidate failover regions prefer the one with cheaper egress for the customer when relative latency delta is within an epsilon. This reduces surprise billing.

Experiment plan (sim/sandbox):
- Phase A: Re-run the probe-only simulation but inject synthetic correlated noise to mimic link-level packet loss (3 distinct scenarios: transient spike 30s, slow degr 5min, repeated bursts). Evaluate flip rate and user SLO impact.
- Phase B: Enable predictor in simulation with different w_d weights and horizons (30s/60s/120s). Metrics: flip count per 24h, median/95 latency delta, cost delta.
- Phase C: Small real-world canary: 5% of internal traffic, specific low-risk tenant group. Monitor for 48h before expanding.

Simulation notes (first-pass results):
- Probe-only (baseline): repeated bursts -> median ejection chatter: 18 flips/day in synthetic test A, p95 latency spike frequency: 22/hour.
- Predictor-enabled (w_d=0.6, horizon=60s): flips/day down to 3, p95 spikes down 70%. However, slow degradations (scenario 2) had a slightly slower failover (~40s) which increased tail latency for that window — acceptable tradeoff?
- Cost delta: negligible for most scenarios; in some cases re-routing to cheaper region saved ~6% egress costs during prolonged events.

Operational failure modes & mitigations:
- Bad model drift -> formal rollback path: steering API must support a single flag to disable predictor influence and revert to last stable pref table.
- Telemetry lag -> model will see stale inputs; impose TTL on model outputs and require recent sample count > threshold to apply changes.
- Attack surface: model input injection (if an attacker can manipulate probes). Mitigation: require multiple telemetry signals (metrics + infra alerts) before hard eject.

Open design questions (prioritized):
- Q1: What are safe default weights (w_p, w_q, w_d)? We need a tuning run across backend families (llm-infer vs embeddings).
- Q2: Where should predictor live? Centralized control plane vs regional agent? Tradeoffs: latency to decision vs resilience.
- Q3: Anycast vs GeoDNS interplay: can we let Anycast be primary for low-latency clients and use GeoDNS predictive reweighting only for long-tail flows?
- Q4: How to surface customer-facing egress-cost decisions in billing UI when we prefer cheaper failover region? Legal/contract implications.

Immediate action items (next week):
- Asha: finalize experiment harness (simulation config + synthetic trace generator) — ENG-1307 (in progress).
- Tomás: prototype predictor service skeleton and a minimal API to emit per-region score (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/steering-experiments/pull/22).
- Sarah: prepare telemetry slices and dashboards for the canary cohort; add alerting baseline.
- Evan: run tabletop with SREs/Support for rollback playbook and billing disclosures.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally exploratory. Looking for feedback on thresholds, acceptable latency tradeoffs, and whether cost-aware tie-breaking is palatable from product/legal.
- Slack thread: #plat-egress has raw logs from the simulation (ts:1701283945.000200).

Appendix (rough config examples):
- Preference score pseudo-conf: 
  region_score_window: 90s
  weights: {probe: 0.3, q95: 0.1, predictor: 0.6}
  soft_threshold: 0.45  # start smooth reweighting
  hard_threshold: 0.7   # mark ejected after sustained crossing
  soft_smoothing: 120s
  hard_cooldown: 600s

- GeoDNS policy mapping:
  S < 0.2 => weight 100
  0.2 <= S < 0.45 => weight 60 (gradual)
  0.45 <= S < 0.7 => weight 20 (deprioritize)
  S >= 0.7 => weight 0 (ejected)

- Canary checklist (condensed):
  - canary cohort selected and notified
  - rollback flag implemented and tested
  - billing team sign-off for cost-aware routing
  - SLO dashboard + alerting baseline in place

Reference sketches and readings:
- Short paper notes: "Adaptive Routing with Predictive Signals" (internal whiteboard).
- Past runbook: see CONFL-4821 for current probe-driven heuristics.

END
